long_biography.plain_text:
Regional autonomy became central to GFL Environmental as Patrick Dovigi expanded the waste-services group. Rather than absorb every acquisition into a single operating centre, the company retained local leaders with responsibility for their markets, preserving regional knowledge inside a larger network.

The structure supported repeated consolidation across solid waste, recycling and environmental services. Independent operators became platforms for further nearby acquisitions, allowing GFL to add density while preserving local accountability. That model turned a fragmented collection of businesses into an integrated provider able to serve customers across several related waste streams.
